Pilot→dragApplications

Drag Pilot to Applications. Then hold Hyper.

Install Pilot 1.0.3.

Free and open source. Needs macOS 27 or later on Apple silicon.

  1. 1DownloadDrag Pilot to Applications
  2. 2Open AnywayOnce, in System Settings › Privacy & Security
  3. 3Pick your Hyper keyAnd allow Accessibility
Details
  1. Download Pilot.dmg, open it and drag Pilot to Applications.
  2. Open Pilot. macOS says Apple could not verify it, because Pilot is open source and not notarized: click Done. Within the hour, open System Settings › Privacy & Security, click Open Anyway beside Pilot and enter your login password.
  3. Pick your Hyper key in Pilot's setup and allow Accessibility. Hyper+Space opens the menu.

Updates install from inside Pilot, signed with the same certificate, so the warning never comes back and your permissions stay.

Permissions, the Terminal route and checking the download

  • Accessibility: Pilot needs it to see your keys and move windows; nothing works without it.
  • Full Disk Access for file search in the menu, and System Events for sleep, restart and dark mode.
  • Microphone for dictation and an AI provider for the AI chat, both optional.
  • Input Monitoring only if Pilot asks, when you bind a mouse's media buttons.
  • Screen Recording when you first take a screenshot or recording, or turn on Menu bar › Other apps › Show exact menu bar items. macOS applies it after Pilot reopens: click Quit & Reopen.

Caps Lock as Hyper: tapped alone it is Escape, and Shift+Caps Lock still types capitals. Password fields are blind to every key tap on macOS, Pilot's included: your binds do not work while one has focus.

From Terminal instead of step 2: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Pilot.app. Check the download against the .sha256 beside it on the Releases page: shasum -a 256 -c Pilot.dmg.sha256.
